# ethereum-optimism/infra Daily Update (Aug 29, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today, a new security-related pull request was opened to update a Go module. Discussions continued on two active issues concerning op-node behavior and Go module consumability.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- A new pull request, [#728](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/728), was opened to update the `golang.org/x/crypto` module to version `v0.55.0` for security purposes.

## CLOSED ISSUES

## NEW ISSUES

## ACTIVE ISSUES

- **Holocene Span Batch Retention in op-node**
  The issue [#22629](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22629) discusses a problem where the op-node's Holocene span-batch stages do not retain a batch when validation returns `BatchUndecided`, leading to `NotEnoughData`. A community member, saintparish4, has offered to pick up this task.

- **op-core/superchain Go Module Consumability**
  Issue [#22678](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22678) highlights that `op-core/superchain` is unconsumable by downstream Go modules because `superchain-configs.zip` is gitignored. User geoknee provided an in-depth analysis, quantifying the storage cost of committing the zip file (approximately 3 MB/year) and comparing it to the current issue of downstream modules being unable to build. The analysis also explored alternatives like loose files and the limitations of embedding directly from submodules. Additionally, geoknee suggested reducing the number of packages that unnecessarily reach the bundle and mentioned a fix in [#22700](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22700) to address accidental dependencies.
